discovery_rules.name: Network interfaces discovery
discovery_rules.description: Used for discovering interfaces from IF-MIB.

item_prototypes.name: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): Inbound packets discarded
item_prototypes.description:
MIB: IF-MIB
The number of inbound packets which were chosen to be discarded even though no errors had been detected to prevent their being deliverable to a higher-layer protocol.
One possible reason for discarding such a packet could be to free up buffer space.
Discontinuities in the value of this counter can occur at re-initialization of the management system and at other times as indicated by the value of `ifCounterDiscontinuityTime`.

item_prototypes.name: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): Inbound packets with errors
item_prototypes.description:
MIB: IF-MIB
For packet-oriented interfaces - the number of inbound packets that contained errors preventing them from being deliverable to a higher-layer protocol.
For character-oriented or fixed-length interfaces - the number of inbound transmission units that contained errors preventing them from being deliverable to a higher-layer protocol.
Discontinuities in the value of this counter can occur at re-initialization of the management system and at other times as indicated by the value of `ifCounterDiscontinuityTime`.

item_prototypes.name: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): Bits received
item_prototypes.description:
MIB: IF-MIB
The total number of octets received on the interface, including framing characters. This object is a 64-bit version of `ifInOctets`.
Discontinuities in the value of this counter can occur at re-initialization of the management system and at other times as indicated by the value of `ifCounterDiscontinuityTime`.

item_prototypes.name: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): Outbound packets discarded
item_prototypes.description:
MIB: IF-MIB
The number of outbound packets which were chosen to be discarded even though no errors had been detected to prevent their being deliverable to a higher-layer protocol.
One possible reason for discarding such a packet could be to free up buffer space.
Discontinuities in the value of this counter can occur at re-initialization of the management system and at other times as indicated by the value of `ifCounterDiscontinuityTime`.

item_prototypes.name: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): Outbound packets with errors
item_prototypes.description:
MIB: IF-MIB
For packet-oriented interfaces - the number of outbound packets that contained errors preventing them from being deliverable to a higher-layer protocol.
For character-oriented or fixed-length interfaces - the number of outbound transmission units that contained errors preventing them from being deliverable to a higher-layer protocol.
Discontinuities in the value of this counter can occur at re-initialization of the management system and at other times as indicated by the value of `ifCounterDiscontinuityTime`.

item_prototypes.name: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): Bits sent
item_prototypes.description:
MIB: IF-MIB
The total number of octets transmitted out of the interface, including framing characters. This object is a 64-bit version of `ifOutOctets`.
Discontinuities in the value of this counter can occur at re-initialization of the management system and at other times as indicated by the value of `ifCounterDiscontinuityTime`.

item_prototypes.name: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): Port state
item_prototypes.description: Operational status, except 8 = shutdown (ifAdminStatus down).

item_prototypes.name: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): Speed
item_prototypes.description:
MIB: IF-MIB
An estimate of the interface's current bandwidth in units of 1,000,000 bits per second.
If this object reports a value of `n`, then the speed of the interface is somewhere in the range of `n-500,000` to `n+499,999`.
For interfaces which do not vary in bandwidth or for those where no accurate estimation can be made, this object should contain the nominal bandwidth.
For a sub-layer which has no concept of bandwidth, this object should be zero.

item_prototypes.name: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): Operational status
item_prototypes.description:
MIB: IF-MIB
The current operational state of the interface.
- The `testing(3)` state indicates that no operational packets can be passed.
- If `ifAdminStatus` is `down(2)`, then `ifOperStatus` should be `down(2)`.
- If `ifAdminStatus` is changed to `up(1)`, then `ifOperStatus` should change to `up(1)` if the interface is ready to transmit and receive network traffic.
- It should change to `dormant(5)` if the interface is waiting for external actions (such as a serial line waiting for an incoming connection).
- It should remain in the `down(2)` state if and only if there is a fault that prevents it from going to the `up(1)` state.
- It should remain in the `notPresent(6)` state if the interface has missing (typically, hardware) components.

trigger_prototypes.expression: {$IFCONTROL:"{#IFNAME}"}=1 and last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.status[ifOperStatus.{#SNMPINDEX}])=2 and (last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.status[ifOperStatus.{#SNMPINDEX}],#1)<>last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.status[ifOperStatus.{#SNMPINDEX}],#2))
trigger_prototypes.name: FortiGate: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): Link down
trigger_prototypes.description:
This trigger expression works as follows:
1. It can be triggered if the operations status is down.
2. `{$IFCONTROL:"{#IFNAME}"}=1` - a user can redefine the context macro to "0", marking this interface as not important. No new trigger will be fired if this interface is down.
3. `{TEMPLATE_NAME:METRIC.diff()}=1` - the trigger fires only if the operational status was up to "1" sometime before.

WARNING: if closed manually - it will not fire again on the next poll, because of `.diff`.

item_prototypes.name: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): Interface type
item_prototypes.description:
MIB: IF-MIB
The type of interface.
Additional values for `ifType` are assigned by the Internet Assigned Numbers Authority (IANA) through updating the syntax of the IANAifType textual convention.

trigger_prototypes.expression:
change(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.speed[ifHighSpeed.{#SNMPINDEX}])<0 and last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.speed[ifHighSpeed.{#SNMPINDEX}])>0 and (
last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.type[ifType.{#SNMPINDEX}])=6 or
last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.type[ifType.{#SNMPINDEX}])=7 or
last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.type[ifType.{#SNMPINDEX}])=11 or
last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.type[ifType.{#SNMPINDEX}])=62 or
last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.type[ifType.{#SNMPINDEX}])=69 or
last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.type[ifType.{#SNMPINDEX}])=117
) and (last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.status[ifOperStatus.{#SNMPINDEX}])<>2)
trigger_prototypes.recovery_expression:
(change(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.speed[ifHighSpeed.{#SNMPINDEX}])>0 and 
last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.speed[ifHighSpeed.{#SNMPINDEX}],#2)>0) or
(last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.status[ifOperStatus.{#SNMPINDEX}])=2)
trigger_prototypes.name: FortiGate: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): Ethernet has changed to lower speed than it was before
trigger_prototypes.description: This Ethernet connection has transitioned down from its known maximum speed. This might be a sign of autonegotiation issues. Acknowledge to close the problem manually.

dependencies.name: FortiGate: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): Link down
dependencies.expression: {$IFCONTROL:"{#IFNAME}"}=1 and last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.status[ifOperStatus.{#SNMPINDEX}])=2 and (last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.status[ifOperStatus.{#SNMPINDEX}],#1)<>last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.status[ifOperStatus.{#SNMPINDEX}],#2))

trigger_prototypes.expression:
(avg(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.in[ifHCInOctets.{#SNMPINDEX}],15m)>({$IF.UTIL.MAX:"{#IFNAME}"}/100)*last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.speed[ifHighSpeed.{#SNMPINDEX}]) or 
avg(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.out[ifHCOutOctets.{#SNMPINDEX}],15m)>({$IF.UTIL.MAX:"{#IFNAME}"}/100)*last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.speed[ifHighSpeed.{#SNMPINDEX}])) and 
last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.speed[ifHighSpeed.{#SNMPINDEX}])>0
trigger_prototypes.recovery_expression:
avg(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.in[ifHCInOctets.{#SNMPINDEX}],15m)<(({$IF.UTIL.MAX:"{#IFNAME}"}-3)/100)*last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.speed[ifHighSpeed.{#SNMPINDEX}]) and 
avg(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.out[ifHCOutOctets.{#SNMPINDEX}],15m)<(({$IF.UTIL.MAX:"{#IFNAME}"}-3)/100)*last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.speed[ifHighSpeed.{#SNMPINDEX}])
trigger_prototypes.name: FortiGate: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): High bandwidth usage
trigger_prototypes.description: The utilization of the network interface is close to its estimated maximum bandwidth.

dependencies.name: FortiGate: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): Link down
dependencies.expression: {$IFCONTROL:"{#IFNAME}"}=1 and last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.status[ifOperStatus.{#SNMPINDEX}])=2 and (last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.status[ifOperStatus.{#SNMPINDEX}],#1)<>last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.status[ifOperStatus.{#SNMPINDEX}],#2))

trigger_prototypes.expression:
min(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.in.errors[ifInErrors.{#SNMPINDEX}],5m)>{$IF.ERRORS.WARN:"{#IFNAME}"}
or min(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.out.errors[ifOutErrors.{#SNMPINDEX}],5m)>{$IF.ERRORS.WARN:"{#IFNAME}"}
trigger_prototypes.recovery_expression:
max(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.in.errors[ifInErrors.{#SNMPINDEX}],5m)<{$IF.ERRORS.WARN:"{#IFNAME}"}*0.8
and max(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.out.errors[ifOutErrors.{#SNMPINDEX}],5m)<{$IF.ERRORS.WARN:"{#IFNAME}"}*0.8
trigger_prototypes.name: FortiGate: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): High error rate
trigger_prototypes.event_name: FortiGate: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): High error rate (>{$IF.ERRORS.WARN:"{#IFNAME}"} for 5m)
trigger_prototypes.description: The trigger recovers when it is below 80% of the `{$IF.ERRORS.WARN:"{#IFNAME}"}` threshold.

dependencies.name: FortiGate: Interface {#IFNAME}({#IFALIAS}): Link down
dependencies.expression: {$IFCONTROL:"{#IFNAME}"}=1 and last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.status[ifOperStatus.{#SNMPINDEX}])=2 and (last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.status[ifOperStatus.{#SNMPINDEX}],#1)<>last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/net.if.status[ifOperStatus.{#SNMPINDEX}],#2))

trigger_prototypes.expression: max(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/pidc.bgp4.state[{#PEER}],5m)<6 and last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/pidc.bgp4.admin[{#PEER}])<>1

trigger_prototypes.description: Not Established for 5 minutes and not shut down on purpose (admin stop); also when the peer has gone from the device's BGP table.

item_prototypes.name: WTP {#WC.NAME}: Administrative status
item_prototypes.description:
MIB: FORTINET-FORTIGATE-MIB
Represents the administrative status of this wireless termination point (WTP).

The following enumerated values are supported:
`discovered(1)` - This WTP was discovered though discovery or join request messages.
`disable(2)` - Controller is configured to not provide service to this WTP.
`enable(3)` - Controller is configured to provide service to this WTP.
`other(0)` - The administration state of the WTP is unknown.

The instance of the object corresponds to the Base MAC Address sub-element in the CAPWAP protocol [RFC5415].

item_prototypes.name: WTP {#WC.NAME}: Connection status
item_prototypes.description:
MIB: FORTINET-FORTIGATE-MIB
Represents the connection status of a WTP to the AC.

The following enumerated values are supported:
`offLine(1)` - The WTP is not connected.
`onLine(2)` - The WTP is connected.
`downloadingImage(3)` - The WTP is downloading software image from the AC on joining.
`connectedImage(4)` - The AC is pushing a software image to the connected WTP.
`other(0)` - The WTP connection status is unknown.

trigger_prototypes.expression: {$WC.STATE.CONTROL:"{#WC.NAME}"}=1 and last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/wc.conn.status[fgWcWtpSessionConnectionState.{#SNMPINDEX}])=1 and (last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/wc.conn.status[fgWcWtpSessionConnectionState.{#SNMPINDEX}],#1)<>last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/wc.conn.status[fgWcWtpSessionConnectionState.{#SNMPINDEX}],#2))
trigger_prototypes.name: FortiGate: WTP {#WC.NAME}: Connection is down
trigger_prototypes.description:

1. It can be triggered if the current connection status is `offLine`.
2. `{$WC.STATE.CONTROL}=1` - a user can redefine the context macro to "0", marking this notification as not important. No new trigger will be fired if this connection is down.

trigger_prototypes.expression: {$WC.UPDATE.CONTROL:"{#WC.NAME}"}=1 and last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/wc.conn.status[fgWcWtpSessionConnectionState.{#SNMPINDEX}])=3 and (last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/wc.conn.status[fgWcWtpSessionConnectionState.{#SNMPINDEX}],#1)<>last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/wc.conn.status[fgWcWtpSessionConnectionState.{#SNMPINDEX}],#2))

trigger_prototypes.expression: {$WC.UPDATE.CONTROL:"{#WC.NAME}"}=1 and last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/wc.conn.status[fgWcWtpSessionConnectionState.{#SNMPINDEX}])=4 and (last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/wc.conn.status[fgWcWtpSessionConnectionState.{#SNMPINDEX}],#1)<>last(/FortiGate by SNMP - PIDC/wc.conn.status[fgWcWtpSessionConnectionState.{#SNMPINDEX}],#2))
